title: Payment Arrangements Budget Review — Income Share Ceilings by Arrangement Type
content:
Two figures of Payment Arrangements govern the budget review: whether the consumer's stated net monthly income must be taken before a plan of the type is set up, and the largest share of that stated income all of the consumer's monthly-equivalent installments may take. A share of 0.0 means the type applies no affordability test.

| Arrangement type | Stated net monthly income taken before set-up | Income share ceiling (percent) |
|---|---|---|
| Promise-to-Pay Arrangement | No | 0.0 |
| Short-Term Installment Plan | No | 0.0 |
| Standard Installment Plan | No | 0.0 |
| Extended Installment Plan | Yes | 20.0 |
| Long-Term Installment Plan | Yes | 15.0 |
| Hardship Reduced-Payment Plan | Yes | 10.0 |

## Desk notes

- The three types that take the stated income are exactly the three that carry a ceiling above 0.0.
- Hypothetical ceiling: for a stated net monthly income of 3000.00, the ceiling reads 600.00 on the Extended Installment Plan (20.0 percent), 450.00 on the Long-Term Installment Plan (15.0 percent) and 300.00 on the Hardship Reduced-Payment Plan (10.0 percent).
